## How do we collaborate when agents write most of the code?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="72%"}
:::: {.sitem .brick}
[🚒]{.emoji} **Why it is hard.** Too many changes to read, private reasoning,
and fewer outside contributors
::::
:::
::: {.column width="28%"}
![](figures/agents-firehose.jpg){height="130px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="A firefighter kneels behind a hose throwing a wide, heavy spray of
water."}
:::
::::

::::: {.challenge-grid .solutions-grid}
:::: {.cbox .teal}
[🎯]{.emoji} **Review intent, not volume**

- A short human statement of what and why
- Small changes, with one person in charge of each
- Regular check-ins on how it is going
::::
:::: {.cbox .slate}
[📓]{.emoji} **A shared lab notebook**

- One entry per line of inquiry
- What was tried, what failed, what is uncertain
::::
:::: {.cbox .brick}
[🙋]{.emoji} **Make the human visible**

- A rationale in the person's own words
- Agent work marked, and "input wanted" flagged
::::
:::: {.cbox .teal}
[🏝️]{.emoji} **Islands with clear boundaries**

- Each person owns their own ecosystem
- Shared low-level tools, custom high-level interfaces
::::
:::: {.cbox .slate}
[🛠️]{.emoji} **Conventions in the tooling**

- A shared agent and skills, agreed by everyone
- Review bots and automated checks catch the rest
::::
:::: {.cbox .grey}
[🚪]{.emoji} **Lower the entry point**

- Tracking issues add a higher layer of conversation above agent and
  human issues
- Work is public by default
- Unequal access is still unsolved
::::
:::::

:::: {.sitem .slate}
[💡]{.emoji} **Learn from software development.** As with much of modern
academic practice, and it is all still in flux
::::
